findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the DC harness page-size to configure (e.g., set `jira.search.views.default.max` to 10 in the container) and the minimum issue count to seed (e.g., ≥25) so the executor can guarantee at least one page-boundary crossing.
evidence: 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages, since the DC page cap is server-configurable and truncation is silent'
No minimum count, no configured page-size value, and no instruction to configure the harness container's page size appear anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan requires 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages' but never specifies the minimum issue count to create nor the DC server's configured page size, leaving an executor unable to determine how many issues to seed without guessing.
findings.location: ### The DC-side mutation suite — 'volume' bullet; AC: 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages'
scenarios: An executor creates 25 issues against a default DC page size of 50 — no page boundary is ever crossed, yet the AC appears satisfied.
Harness defaults to 100 per page; executor creates 50 issues; pagination is never exercised; the very defect the plan cites (`get_parent_map`) goes undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: In the volume bullet and matching AC, add: 'Configure the DC harness with a page size of 10 (via `jira.search.views.default.max=10` in `jira-config.properties`); seed at least 25 issues, guaranteeing ≥3 pagination pages.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider sequencing a thin vertical-slice milestone (1 inbound + 1 outbound mutation + isolation assertions) that de-risks the harness/store-copy setup before adding the full 13-mutation comprehensive suite, so setup defects don't block all signal.
evidence: 'create issue; edit summary; edit description; transition status; add label; remove label; add comment; edit comment; assign; unassign; create issue link; delete issue link; set sub-task parent; clear parent; delete issue (absence probe)'
No staged sequencing is described: all mutations are bundled into a single deliverable alongside the isolation harness and store-copy setup.
G5 sequencing sub-criterion: 'thin vertical-slice / evidence-gated MVP de-risking the riskiest piece first, not a horizontal big-bang'
findings.finding: The plan goes directly to a comprehensive 13+ mutation suite (inbound, outbound, volume/pagination, idempotence) rather than sequencing a thin vertical-slice MVP first. While all mutations serve one coherent goal, the riskiest unknown — whether the harness + store-copy + isolation setup itself works — is not de-risked before the full mutation suite is added. If the isolation or store-copy setup fails, the entire suite is blocked rather than a subset delivering early signal.
findings.location: 'The DC-side mutation suite' section; Acceptance criteria — comprehensive list of 13+ inbound+outbound mutations
scenarios: The `git init` + store-copy + scrub machinery has a subtle bug; the entire 13-mutation suite is blocked rather than a 2-mutation MVP delivering early proof.
The DC harness itself has a compatibility issue with one of the 13 mutation types; diagnosing which mechanism failed is harder when all are introduced simultaneously.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] The `jira-dc-harness` CI job must explicitly fetch/checkout the `tickets` branch (e.g., `git fetch origin tickets && git worktree add` or `git checkout tickets`) before the store-copy step, since `.tickets-tracker/` is gitignored and absent from the default `actions/checkout` working tree.
evidence: .gitignore line 9: `.tickets-tracker/` is gitignored, so `actions/checkout` does NOT populate it
The ticket store lives on an orphan `tickets` branch (README.md: 'orphan branch (worktree at `.tickets-tracker/`)')
The plan describes 'git init a fresh repo and copies the ticket-store content in' but provides no mechanism (e.g., `git fetch origin tickets && git checkout tickets`) for obtaining that content in CI
tests/external/conftest.py:167 — the existing rebar_repo fixture calls rebar.init_repo() on an empty dir; the plan's 'copy' requires a separate, unspecified fetch step
findings.finding: The plan says the CI job 'git inits a fresh repo and copies the ticket-store content in,' but `.tickets-tracker/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:9`) and the orphan `tickets` branch is not present in a standard `actions/checkout`. The plan never specifies the step that fetches or checks out the `tickets` branch to supply the content being copied. Without this step the 'copy of this project's real ticket store' is empty, reproducing the exact `scanned=0` failure the plan exists to fix.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Run the live verification against a COPY OF THIS PROJECT'S ACTUAL TICKET STORE'; Scope section — 'the `jira-dc-harness` job gains the store-copy step'
scenarios: CI runner runs `actions/checkout`, gets working tree with no `.tickets-tracker/` content, CI job `git init`s the copy repo and has nothing to copy in, pass sees `scanned=0` — the exact failure the plan was written to fix
findings.suggested_fix: Add a CI step before the store-copy that materialises the ticket store: e.g., `git fetch origin tickets:tickets` in the main checkout, then copy `.tickets-tracker/` content into the freshly `git init`-ed isolation repo.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify the `sync.remote` isolation AC: the assertion should check that no git remote named by `sync.remote` exists in the repo (i.e., `git remote get-url $(config.sync.remote)` fails), not that the config value itself is empty — since `sync.remote` defaults to `'origin'` and will never be an empty string.
evidence: src/rebar/_config_schema.py:307: `remote: str = "origin"  # git remote the tickets branch syncs to`
A fresh `git init` repo with default config will have `sync.remote = 'origin'` — the config key is not empty, the git remote is absent
Plan text: 'a test fails the job if `git remote` returns anything in the working repo, or if `sync.remote` resolves to a non-empty value'
findings.finding: The plan's AC asserts 'if `sync.remote` resolves to a non-empty value' as a failure condition, but `sync.remote` defaults to `'origin'` in `_config_schema.py:307` even when no git remote named `origin` exists. The config key is always `'origin'` unless explicitly overridden; the plan conflates a non-empty config value with an actual live push remote. The assertion as literally written would always fail (the value is always `'origin'`) or requires an explicit `sync.remote = ''` override in the copied repo's `rebar.toml`.
findings.location: AC line: '`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off` and an empty `sync.remote` are both asserted in the same test'
scenarios: Implementer writes `assert config.sync.remote == ''` — always fails because the default is `'origin'`
Implementer writes `assert not git_remote_exists(config.sync.remote)` — passes, but that is a different assertion than what the AC text specifies
The actual safety property (no push remote exists) is correctly captured by `git remote` being empty, but the `sync.remote` assertion requires clarification
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'an empty `sync.remote`' with 'no git remote named by `sync.remote` is registered in the working repo' (i.e., `git remote` output is empty, OR `git remote get-url origin` fails). The primary isolation mechanism (no git remote) already covers this — the `sync.remote` check is the belt to the suspenders, not a config-value emptiness check.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the DC mutation step must create at least `page_size + 1` issues on the DC harness (default 100 for `get_parent_map`; confirm the harness's actual cap via `/rest/api/2/configuration` or a probe), and assert that the fetcher made more than one page request — do not rely on the real store copy's local-ticket count to drive DC-side pagination.
evidence: Plan: 'volume: enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages, since the DC page cap is server-configurable and truncation is silent'
Plan: 'the pass sees realistic volume ... from this project's ACTUAL TICKET STORE' — but this is LOCAL volume, not DC-harness volume
transport.py:503: `page_size = 100` for get_parent_map; transport.py:376: `max_results: int = 50` for search_issues
The DC harness starts empty — it has no pre-existing issues. Only the DC mutation suite creates issues there.
get_parent_map docstring (transport.py:484-542) documents exactly this truncation-silencing bug, which J11 is supposed to prove is fixed: without >page_size DC-side issues it is untestable.
findings.finding: The pagination AC ('run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages') cannot be met by the described mechanism. The plan attributes pagination exercise to 'realistic volume' from the real store copy, but pagination in the DC reconciler is a property of the FETCHER calling the DC harness (transport.search_issues / transport.get_parent_map against the live Docker container), not of the local ticket count. The DC harness starts empty; unless the DC mutation suite creates more issues than the transport's page_size (100 for get_parent_map per transport.py:503, 50 for search_issues per transport.py:376), the fetcher never exercises a second page. The plan never specifies that the mutation suite must create enough DC-side issues to cross the page boundary.
findings.location: ## The DC-side mutation suite / bullet 'volume' / AC 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages'
scenarios: Implementer creates 5-10 DC issues for the mutation suite (sufficient for inbound/outbound probes), runs the suite, and the pagination AC silently passes because there is never a second page — the same 'converged' / 'works' ambiguity J11 was written to prevent, now applied to pagination.
findings.suggested_fix: In the 'volume' bullet of the DC mutation suite, replace 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages' with a concrete lower bound tied to the harness's known/probed page cap, and add a step that creates that many issues on the DC harness before the inbound pass runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that the pagination AC is grounded in DC-SIDE issue count: either the mutation suite explicitly creates > (configured DC page cap) issues in the harness project, or the test asserts the harness project issue count exceeds the page boundary before claiming pagination was exercised.
evidence: Plan: 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages, since the DC page cap is server-configurable and truncation is silent'
Jira DC REST API v2 pagination default is 50 per page (maxResults=50); the cap is admin-configurable per Atlassian docs
The plan relies on the real project ticket store for volume but never asserts a minimum issue count, nor does it mandate creating synthetic issues to guarantee crossing the page boundary

If the harness project key receives only the issues created by the mutation suite (< page_size), the pagination path is never exercised regardless of the local store size — pagination is on the DC side (the harness project), not the local store copy
findings.finding: The plan asserts the copied store will contain 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages,' but the DC harness image (Jira 8.17.1) defaults to 50 results per page and the page cap is server-configurable. The plan never verifies or asserts that the real project ticket store actually contains more than (page_cap × 2) tickets, meaning the pagination-coverage AC could pass vacuously if the store has fewer issues than the DC server's page limit.
findings.location: ## The DC-side mutation suite / volume bullet; AC: 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages, so silent truncation cannot pass'
scenarios: The real project store has N local tickets but the harness Jira project receives only the mutation-suite's handful of issues — pagination never triggers and the silent-truncation defect class is not exercised
A future run where the mutation suite is incomplete creates fewer issues than the DC page cap, causing the pagination AC to report vacuous pass
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step in the mutation suite that creates at least (page_size + 1) issues in the harness DC project (e.g., a bulk-create loop of 55 issues before the targeted mutation tests), then assert that at least 2 pages were fetched by checking that the reconciler's inbound pass scanned > page_cap issues.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact issue count to create in the dc_mutations suite AND either (a) document the atlas-run Jira 8.17.1 default maxResults cap and prove the chosen count exceeds it, or (b) add a Jira system-property override (`-Djira.search.views.default.max=N`) in the Dockerfile/docker-compose so the cap is known and the test volume is calibrated against it.
evidence: Plan text: 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages, since the DC page cap is server-configurable and truncation is silent'
transport.py get_parent_map uses page_size=100; search_issues uses max_results=50
No issue count or harness page-size configuration is specified in the plan or in docker-compose.yml

Partially-verified: transport pagination logic is unit-proven correct (test_get_parent_map_survives_server_side_maxresults_truncation uses SERVER_CAP=20 with 250 issues); the live page threshold for the atlas-run instance is unspecified
findings.finding: The plan's AC requires the run to exercise 'MULTIPLE pagination pages', but neither the number of issues to create nor the Jira 8.17.1 atlas-run container's effective maxResults cap is specified. The DC transport's `search_issues` uses `maxResults=50` by default and `get_parent_map` uses 100; if the test creates fewer issues than the server's page cap, the run will never hit a second page and the pagination AC passes vacuously — exactly the silent-truncation class the plan says it must prevent. The existing unit test proves the pagination LOGIC, but it does not substitute for the live pagination exercise the plan mandates.
findings.location: DC mutation suite / AC: 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages, so silent truncation cannot pass'
scenarios: The dc_mutations fixture creates N issues where N < default harness maxResults; all fit in one page; get_parent_map and search_issues each make a single call; the pagination loop exits after one batch; the AC is asserted green despite never exercising the multi-page path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `JIRA_SEARCH_MAX_RESULTS` override (e.g., `-Djira.search.views.default.max=5`) to the atlas-run JVM args in the Dockerfile so the page cap is deterministically small, then create at least 6 issues in the mutation suite — this guarantees multiple pages without creating hundreds of issues.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete pagination assertion: after the inbound pass, assert that the reconciler's scan count equals the number of seeded issues (e.g., `scanned == N`), which fails if any page was silently dropped.
evidence: The plan lists this as an AC but provides no test assertion, log-line check, counter, or API-call trace that would confirm the paginator was exercised.
VERIFY-COMMAND DEFECT TAXONOMY item 4 (fixture invalidity): seeding N issues is the fixture; it does not itself exercise the claim that the paginator fetched page 2+.
The cited defect (`get_parent_map`) was a silent truncation — by definition it produced no error output, so absence-of-exception is insufficient proof.
findings.finding: The AC 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages' has no described proving command or assertion mechanism — creating enough issues is a necessary precondition but does not itself prove the paginator was invoked and returned results across page boundaries.
findings.location: AC: 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages, so silent truncation cannot pass'
scenarios: Executor seeds 25 issues, reconciler fetches page 1 only (bug), the test sees all 25 returned (if page size > 25) and passes; or worse, sees only 10 but doesn't assert count matches seeded count.
A refactored paginator regresses to page-1-only; the AC passes because no exception is thrown.
findings.suggested_fix: In the volume AC, add: 'Assert `scanned` in reconciler output equals the exact number of seeded issues; a mismatch indicates silent truncation. Additionally assert at least one log line or transport counter shows page_index >= 2 was fetched.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly enumerate the outbound mutation suite (matching the inbound list item-for-item) so that 'every mutation in the suite above' has an unambiguous, auditable meaning for both implementer and reviewer.
evidence: AC quote: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line'
Approach quote: 'outbound (local -> DC): the mirror set, driven by local ticket edits' — no explicit list provided, unlike the inbound direction which enumerates ~13 named operations
findings.finding: The AC 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually' references 'the mirror set' for outbound mutations, but the outbound suite is never explicitly enumerated — only described as 'the mirror set, driven by local ticket edits.' The verify step is underspecified: an implementer and a reviewer cannot agree on whether the outbound assertion set is complete.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips'; Approach — 'outbound (local -> DC): the mirror set, driven by local ticket edits'
scenarios: Implementer asserts only a subset of outbound mutations and the AC passes because 'the mirror set' is undefined — silent truncation of test coverage identical to the pagination bug the plan is designed to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the mirror set, driven by local ticket edits' with an explicit bulleted list mirroring the inbound list: edit summary; edit description; transition status; add label; remove label; add comment; edit comment; assign; unassign; create issue link; delete issue link; set sub-task parent; clear parent; delete local issue (absence probe on DC).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the pagination volume is determined: either query the DC harness's configured page size at test setup and assert `issue_count > page_size`, or hard-code a conservative lower bound (e.g., 55 issues) and document the assumption — do not leave 'enough' undefined.
evidence: 'volume: enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages, since the DC page cap is server-configurable and truncation is silent' — acknowledged as server-configurable but no concrete issue count or page-size probe is specified
The DC page cap is called out as server-configurable, meaning the correct threshold cannot be hardcoded safely without first querying the server's actual setting
findings.finding: The 'enough issues to force MULTIPLE pagination pages' volume threshold is unspecified and not configurable. If the DC harness container's default page size differs from the assumed value, the suite may create fewer issues than one page and never exercise pagination — silently passing the pagination AC while the defect it targets remains undetected.
findings.location: Approach / 'The DC-side mutation suite' section; AC 'the run exercises MULTIPLE pagination pages'
scenarios: DC harness defaults to page size 50; suite creates 30 issues; pagination is never triggered; the AC is asserted satisfied but the `get_parent_map` class of bug remains uncaught
findings.suggested_fix: At test setup, query the DC harness `/rest/api/2/configuration` (or equivalent) to read `maxResults`; create `max_results + 5` issues and assert the suite confirms at least two pages were fetched. Alternatively, configure the DC harness container to use a small page size (e.g., 5) via `jira.search.maxResults` JVM property and create 12 issues.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that round-trip assertions for each mutation must read ACTUAL STATE from an independent oracle (local ticket YAML/git tree for inbound; DC REST API response for outbound) — not solely the reconciler's subprocess output — so a reconciler that logs success but writes wrong data still fails the test.
evidence: Plan text: 'each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line' — specifies the form of assertion (per-mutation, not aggregate) but not the SOURCE of ground truth for that assertion

Plan text: 'zero unhandled exceptions, asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams' — subprocess stream parsing is established as the primary assertion channel, creating the risk that all mutation assertions also use this channel
ABSENCE: the plan never requires post-pass queries to the local ticket store (git tree reads, YAML field checks) or independent DC API queries to verify field values survived the round-trip correctly
The operator-attested ACs ('appears in local store', 'appears on DC issue') imply independent observation for two mutations; the remaining ~20 mutations in the suite have no such specification
findings.finding: The plan requires that each mutation in the DC suite is 'asserted individually' but never specifies that the assertion oracle must read the LOCAL STORE or DC INSTANCE state INDEPENDENTLY of the reconciler's own output. If assertions are implemented by parsing the reconciler's subprocess streams (its own log lines such as 'synced 1 issue'), the tests become self-authored oracles: the reconciler reports success, the test reads that report, and the suite goes green even when the reconciler silently misroutes a field, skips a sub-task link, or maps a status incorrectly. This is the classic tautology — the reconciler attests to its own correctness.
findings.location: AC line: 'every mutation in the suite above round-trips, each asserted individually rather than by an aggregate converged line'; section 'The DC-side mutation suite'
scenarios: Reconciler logs 'processed REBAR-42' but writes the wrong description field — test passes because it reads the log, not the YAML file
Status transition is recorded in reconciler output but the local ticket YAML still has the old status — test misses the bug
Comment edit round-trip: reconciler reports 'comment synced' but DC still shows the original comment — log-based assertion is blind to this
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'For each inbound mutation, post-pass verification reads the local ticket store (git-tracked YAML files) directly and asserts the field value matches what was set in DC; for each outbound mutation, post-pass verification queries the DC REST API directly and asserts the DC issue field matches the local edit — neither direction is verified solely by parsing reconciler log output.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define 'mass deletion' with a concrete threshold (e.g., 'planned deletions > 10% of scanned ticket count, or > 20 absolute, whichever is smaller') so the assertion can be written unambiguously.
evidence: 'mass deletion' appears without a numeric threshold or formula (e.g., >N, or >X% of copied store size)
The plan itself notes the leftover prev_snapshot drives 'deletion path across hundreds of local tickets', implying 'mass' is a large count — but this is context, not a definition.
An executor must decide whether mass means >0, >10, or >50% to write the assertion.
findings.finding: The AC 'the first inbound pass is asserted NOT to plan a mass deletion' uses the undefined term 'mass', making the assertion threshold unknowable and the criterion unmeasurable as written.
findings.location: AC: 'the first inbound pass is asserted NOT to plan a mass deletion — that is the observable signature of a leftover prev_snapshot.json'
scenarios: The assertion is written as deletions_planned > 0, which would fail any run where even one issue is legitimately absent from the harness.
The assertion is written as deletions_planned > 100, missing the case where a small but real leftover snapshot affects a lightly-populated copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'NOT to plan a mass deletion' with 'NOT to plan deletion of more than 2 local tickets (the harness has no retired issues, so any deletion > 2 is a setup artifact)' — or whatever invariant holds for the harness state.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item "this project's live Jira is untouched: the suite never resolves a non-harness ba" cites operational evidence (live_run) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the idempotence observable explicitly (e.g., 'both `outbound_differ total` and `inbound_differ total` equal 0 in the second pass's structured output, AND no new git commit is created in the working repo') so the assertion can be written without ambiguity.
evidence: 'writes nothing' is not defined against any artifact, log field, or API-call trace.
The plan's own example output shows 'outbound_differ total=0 inbound_differ total=0' — this is a candidate observable but is not referenced in the AC.
Without naming the observable, an executor could assert only 'no exception raised', which is weaker than idempotence.
findings.finding: The AC 'a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing (idempotence)' names no concrete observable to measure — it is unclear whether 'writes nothing' means outbound_differ total=0, no git commits created, no HTTP write calls made, or some combination, leaving the assertion undefined.
findings.location: AC: 'a repeated pass after each direction writes nothing (idempotence)'; also mutation suite bullet: 'idempotence: an immediately repeated pass after each direction writes nothing'
scenarios: Executor asserts no exception on the second pass and marks idempotence AC green, while the reconciler actually re-writes fields to their existing values (a real idempotence bug that produces no exception).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'writes nothing' with: 'outbound_differ total=0 AND inbound_differ total=0 in the repeated pass log (parsed from structured output), AND `git log --oneline` shows no new commit in the working repo relative to before the repeated pass.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the error-handling contract for the `dc_mutations` helper: at minimum specify that any DC API call failure aborts the suite immediately with a clear diagnostic (not a downstream assertion error), and that each mutation step is wrapped with a timeout so a slow container cannot silently stall the job.
evidence: The plan enumerates 14+ DC-side mutation operations but says nothing about what happens when any individual mutation call fails
'zero unhandled exceptions, asserted on the reconciler subprocess streams' — this covers the reconciler subprocess but not the mutation helper's own HTTP calls
ABSENCE: no retry, timeout, or cleanup-on-failure logic is described for the `dc_mutations` helper
findings.finding: No error-handling or abort strategy is specified for failures in the DC mutation helper (e.g., a DC API call to create an issue or add a comment returns a 4xx/5xx mid-suite). A partial mutation sequence leaves the DC harness in an inconsistent state, making subsequent round-trip assertions unreliable — and the failure may surface as a spurious assertion error rather than a clean test failure.
findings.location: Approach / 'The DC-side mutation suite' section; `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` scope entry
scenarios: DC container is briefly overloaded; 'add comment' call returns 503; subsequent 'edit comment' mutation fires against an absent comment; assertion failure message is misleading about the actual defect
Mutation sequence partially completes; idempotence pass fires against inconsistent harness state and produces false positives

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that verifies the README exists and covers the auto-push isolation contract (e.g. 'a `README.md` exists in `tests/external/live_jira_dc/` and documents the auto-push risk and each isolation layer').
evidence: Scope bullet: '`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md` — document the isolation contract and WHY (auto-push)'
ABSENCE: no AC names or verifies the README
findings.finding: The README (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md`) is listed as an explicit Scope deliverable ('document the isolation contract and WHY (auto-push)') but no acceptance criterion covers its existence, content, or correctness — it is an orphaned deliverable.
findings.location: Scope section — third bullet; Acceptance criteria section (no matching AC)
scenarios: An implementer could ship everything else, skip the README, and pass all ACs — the isolation contract rationale (auto-push risk) is never documented, defeating stated purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: '`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md` exists and documents (a) the auto-push risk, (b) each of the four isolation layers, and (c) why the scrub must glob `.bridge_state*` rather than a hardcoded list.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an ADR or an AGENTS.md entry capturing the decision to use a real-store copy as the test fixture, the invariants it depends on (artifact glob pattern, no-production-key assertion), and the tradeoffs versus synthetic data — the README alone is insufficient for a project-wide architectural decision.
evidence: 'document the isolation contract and WHY (auto-push)' — the README scope is limited to isolation rationale
ABSENCE: no ADR or AGENTS.md update is mentioned for the decision to couple test realism to the live store shape
The plan itself notes this is a novel fixture approach: 'Run the live verification against a COPY OF THIS PROJECT'S ACTUAL TICKET STORE' — a departure from the prior `rebar_repo` fixture pattern
findings.finding: The novel architectural decision — using a copy of the real project ticket store as a live test fixture (rather than synthetic/generated data) — is proposed to be documented only in a test-local README (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md`). findings.finding: The outbound pass mechanism has a hidden ordering dependency that is not specified. The AC '[operator-attested] a local edit appears on the DC issue after an outbound pass' requires a confirmed binding between a local ticket and a DC issue key. After the scrub (which removes all bindings.json entries) and against a fresh empty DC harness, no bindings exist — the outbound differ would compute zero mutations, repeating the 'outbound_differ total=0' failure the plan was created to prevent. The plan's mutation suite lists inbound and outbound as a flat enumeration without specifying that the outbound suite must target tickets that were FIRST adopted via an inbound pass (which is the only way bindings are created when starting from a scrubbed state).
